summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — HAS +12%, EFX +11%, CRL +6%, IT +6%, MSCI +5%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (GM -7%, DVA -6%, GPC -6%, FIX -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HAS (+11.82%) — Hasbro reported Q3 2026 results on Oct 20 after the close. Magic: The Gathering passed $600M in quarterly revenue, the 2026 outlook was raised and the buyback target doubled. The stock gapped up on Oct 21. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: HAS is a mid-cap consumer/toy name that no strategy covers. It was also an overnight earnings gap, so the move was set at the open and a post-open momentum signal would have come too late.

top_movers.catalyst: Hasbro reported Q3 2026 results on Oct 20 after the close. Magic: The Gathering passed $600M in quarterly revenue, the 2026 outlook was raised and the buyback target doubled. The stock gapped up on Oct 21.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HAS is a mid-cap consumer/toy name that no strategy covers. It was also an overnight earnings gap, so the move was set at the open and a post-open momentum signal would have come too late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap consumer discretionary names with earnings in the prior 24h to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings gate release names gapping up 8% or more on at least 2x average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely Q3 2026 earnings reaction: results reported Oct 20 showed revenue of $1.693B (+10%), with mortgage +15% and USIS +13%, after July's guidance-driven selloff. I couldn't find coverage of the Oct 21 price move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: EFX is a mid/large-cap credit-bureau (business services) name. The move was an earnings-gap rebound, so any momentum or news filter would have seen it only after the open gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap financial/business-services names to the universe, and let the earnings gate release post-earnings gaps of +8% or more with volume above 1.5× average on day 2, after the opening range settles.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found for 10/21 (Q3 earnings are due Nov 4); likely a sector move in CROs/life-science tools, possibly peer results or biotech funding sentiment. This is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CRL is a mid-cap (~$15B) healthcare CRO/life-science tools name, and no strategy includes it. With no clear catalyst, a +6% sector-driven move would also not have triggered news-reactive entries.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic 'top-gainer scan' to the momentum universe, admitting S&P 400/500 healthcare names with a gap/close move ≥ +5% on volume ≥ 1.5× the 20-day average, so mid-cap sector rotations are tradable.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news catalyst found. Gartner has been rebounding since its Aug 2026 Q2 beat, so this looks like a continued AI-disruption-fear relief rally in research and software names.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Gartner is a mid-cap research and consulting stock, outside the bot's configured lists. With no earnings or gap trigger, a news-reactive filter would also have had nothing to fire on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unlisted mover scan' that lets any US stock above ~$5B market cap and ~$50M average daily dollar volume into the momentum-trader candidate pool when it closes up ≥4% on ≥1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-Q3 earnings reaction. MSCI reported Oct 20 with adj EPS $5.11 vs ~$5.02 est, revenue $892M (+12.4%) vs ~$884M est, and asset-based fees +24.9%. I couldn't confirm the price reaction itself.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MSCI is a ~$45B mid/large-cap financial-data/index provider that no strategy lists. The move was an earnings gap, so pre-market positioning would have beaten any post-open momentum signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap financial data/index names (MSCI, SPGI, MCO, FDS) to the momentum universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a post-results gap of at least +4% on volume of at least 1.5x average.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 beat (adj EPS $2.50 vs ~$2.39), FY26 EPS guide raised to $9.10–9.15, plus an expanded Amazon data-center deal (warrant for 3.2M shares). Articles date the pop to Oct 20, so the bot's window may lag by a day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MMM is a large-cap industrial that no strategy lists. It was also an earnings/deal gap that happened pre-market, so a post-open momentum or news-reactive entry would have missed the move.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap industrials like MMM to the momentum universe, and let the earnings-gate release names that gap up ≥+4% on a guidance raise, entering within 30 minutes of the open if volume is ≥1.5× average.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-Q3 earnings selloff: GM reported Oct 20 and narrowed its FY26 guidance. The stock fell about 7% the next day despite a new $20B buyback. I couldn't find coverage naming the cause, so the cause is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: GM is a large-cap cyclical auto name that no strategy covers. It was also an earnings-gap move, which a momentum or mean-reversion filter would likely skip, and the bot has no short capability for a gap-down.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap autos/cyclicals (GM, F) to the mean-reversion universe, with an earnings-gate release for gap-downs ≥5% on ≥2× average volume once the first 30 minutes after the open have passed.

top_movers.catalyst: Fell ~6.4% on a new HHS/Trump administration kidney-care proposal aimed at dialysis-market competition, plus pre-earnings de-risking before the Oct 29 Q3 report. Press dates the drop Oct 20.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DVA is a mid-cap healthcare-services stock. The drop was a policy-headline gap with no earnings print, so momentum and mean-reversion filters would not have flagged it, and the bot has no short capability.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a healthcare-policy watchlist (DVA, FMS, CMS-exposed names) to the news-reactive universe, triggered by an HHS/CMS headline plus a ≥5% single-day drop on ≥1.5× average volume, and use it as a risk-off or avoid flag. No short entry is needed.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-Q3 earnings selloff: GPC reported Oct 20 and narrowed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.50-7.75 (top end cut from $8.00). I couldn't confirm the Q3 figures or the Oct 21 price reaction.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: GPC is a mid-cap auto/industrial parts distributor. The drop was an earnings-gap move that came after the print, so momentum and news-reactive entries had no pre-market position. A long-only bot has no short exposure to a guidance cut.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap consumer/industrial distributors to the mean-reversion universe and add a post-earnings-drift rule: after a gap-down of 5% or more on an earnings day, watch for a rebound entry once the next session's volume confirms.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found; likely profit-taking and rotation out of AI/data-center construction names ahead of Q3 earnings (FIX trades ~60x earnings, with past drops tied to insider selling).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FIX is a ~$50B mid/large-cap industrial/HVAC contractor that no strategy lists. With no discrete catalyst, a news-reactive bot had nothing to trigger on, and a -5% drift on a sector move would not pass a momentum filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FIX and peers (EME, STRL, PWR) to a 'data-center-capex' basket in the mean-reversion universe, entering only when a ≥5% drop comes with no earnings or news flag and RSI(14) is below 35.
